what_is_said: Dharma Sabha at Rampur Beauleah maintains Purāṇic orthodoxy against the Brahma Samaj, publishes a weekly, 'several thousand members' (1871); Rajshahi Brahma Samaj founded 1859
quote: The Dharma Sabha at Rémpur Beau- leah is an institution established for the maintenance of orthedox Hinduism, as laid down in the Purdns; in opposition to the Bréhma Samé4j

volume: Hunter, Statistical Account of Bengal VIII: Bogra [wbsl.19253]
what_is_said: Introduced 1858 by a schoolmaster; once c.60, now not more than 20
quote: Its actual followers, though once numbering about sixty, are now not more than twenty.
notes: Bogra 1910 (BG22, p. 31): 23 Brahmos (1901), new pakka Samaj building, Magh utsab per Sadharan ritual, many educated Hindus hold similar theistic views

volume: Hunter, Statistical Account of Bengal IX: Murshidabad, Pabna [wbsl.19217]
what_is_said: Berhampore: c.50 members (1870), prayer meetings from 1861 despite 'considerable opposition from the old orthodox Hindu party', Adi Samaj liturgy, library; Pabna: 1856 attempt, refounded 1864, c.8 members (1876). Same page: Sannyasis 190 (1872 census)
quote: despite considerable opposition from the old orthodox Hindu party, the Brdhma Samdj has continued to hold its meetings with regularity.
notes: juxtaposes Brahmos with 190 'Sivaite' Sannyasis in Murshidabad

volume: Hunter, Statistical Account of Bengal II: Nadiya, Jessor [in.ernet.dli.2015.14586]
institution: Brahma Samaj centres; Sanatan Dharma Rakshini Sabha
what_is_said: Nadiya Brahmos c.200; centres at Krishnagar, Ranaghat, Santipur, Kushtia; at Ranaghat a Sanatan Dharma Rakshini Sabha 'for the preservation of orthodox idolatrous Hinduism'; Jessore Samaj c.1858 met behind closed doors under public pressure
quote: At Rdn%h^t there is a San^tan Dharma Rakshini Sabh^, an opposition institution for the preserva- tion of orthodox idolatrous Hinduism.
notes: sanatan_dharma counter-society

volume: Hunter, Statistical Account of Bengal III: Hugli [in.ernet.dli.2015.39535]
place: Howrah, Konnagar, Basudha, Baluti, Baidyabati, Chinsurah, Hugli, Chandernagore
what_is_said: Only 6 returned as Brahmos in 1872 census, but the Collector (1870) estimated c.1,200 followers; settlements in towns, little hold on rural population
quote: The Collector of the District, in 1870, estimated the number of Brdhma Samdj followers in Hdgli District at about 1200.
notes: Calcutta-area; duplicate scan .534064

volume: Hunter, Statistical Account of Bengal I: 24 Parganas [in.ernet.dli.2015.17070]
what_is_said: The Samaj recruited principally from Calcutta town; description reserved for the Calcutta account; very few Brahmos in the rural district
quote: The Brahma Samaj is principally recruited from the town, and I accordingly reserve my description of it for my Statistical Account of C^ r " Ha The number of Brahmas in the rural part of the District is very small.
notes: Calcutta-area

volume: Hunter, Statistical Account of Bengal XVIII: Cuttack, Balasor [in.ernet.dli.2015.38535]
what_is_said: Cuttack Samaj est. 1856, c.40 members in city (1870); Balasor congregation Oct 1869, 4 → 19 in six months, then decline
quote: in 1870 the Collector reported to me that the society numbered about forty members in Cuttack city, but that it made no progress outside the town.

volume: Hunter, Statistical Account of Bengal (Bihar vols XI–XVI) [in.ernet.dli.2015.42971]
district: Patna, Saran, Gaya, Hazaribagh, Monghyr, Tirhut
what_is_said: Restricted to Bengali residents: Gaya 15 (all Bengalis), Hazaribagh 20 (all natives of Bengal, government employ), Patna Bengalis only with Bihari 'secret sympathisers'; none in Tirhut/Manbhum
quote: The Brahma SamAj, or reformed theistic sect of Hindus, numbers 20 adherents in the District. Without an exception they are natives of Bengal Proper.
page: Hazaribagh p. 85; Gaya p. 41; Patna p. 64
notes: grouped row covering HU11, HU12, HU13, HU15, HU16, HU17

what_is_said: Santiniketan, Debendranath Tagore's retreat, endowed as a hermitage with Adi Samaj liturgy by an appointed Brahman, animal food banned; Rabindranath's Brahma Vidyalaya boarding school 'on the old Hindu ascetic lines'; Samajes at Suri and Nalhati; Sadharan Brahmo Samaj ran famine relief
quote: At Bhubandanga, a mile to the west, is a Brahrao Samaj building known as the Santiniketan abode of peace) of Bolpnr, -which is associated with the life of the great Brahmo leader Devendra Nath Tagore.

what_is_said: Radhanagar (Raghunathpur) home of Raja Rammohan Rai, founder of the Brahmo Samaj; the Tattvabodhini Sabha school (200 boys, 1843) lost pupils because 'some of the boys became Vedantists'; Brahmos 26 in 1901 census
quote: the Tatwabodhiui Sabha of Calcutta, the origiaal name of the modem Ath Br^ma Samaj, had in 1843 a flourishing school with 200 boys ; but as some of the boys became Yedautists, many parents withdrew their sons
notes: 'Vedantist' = Brahmo here (Debendranath's Vedāntic phase), not Śaṅkara order; Calcutta-area. No Ramakrishna/Kamarpukur mention in this volume

what_is_said: 88 Brahmos in district (1911); Garifa birthplace of Keshab Chandra Sen 'founder of the Brahmo Samaj' (sic, b. 1838); Dakshineswar described only as Rani Rasmani's Navaratna temples (Kali and Krishna, 12 Siva shrines) with no mention of Ramakrishna
quote: this village was the birth-place of Keshab Chandra Sen, the founder of the Brahmo Samaj (born in 1838).
notes: Calcutta-area; silence on Ramakrishna at Dakshineswar notable

what_is_said: Mission founded 1897 by Ramakrishna's disciples with Vivekananda as head; Belur math; centres listed: Calcutta (Udbodhan), Bhabda (Murshidabad orphanage), Benares, Mayavati (Prabuddha Bharata), Kankhal sevashrama, Madras (Brahmavadin), Bangalore; famine relief 1908 round Chilka lake in 26 villages; no census figures (followers returned as Hindus); orange-robed celibate ascetics; fairs at Belur (birth tithi) and Kankurgachhi
quote: the Ramkrishna Mission, which has its headquarters at : Belur in this district, and was founded in 1897 by the disciples of Ramkrishna Paramhansa with Swami Vivekananda as their head
notes: compiled from a note sent by Swami Sivananda of Belur; duplicate scan in.ernet.dli.2015.206872

what_is_said: Quotes Max Müller: Ramakrishna preached the old religion founded on the Upanishads, systematised in Bādarāyaṇa's Sūtras 'and finally developed in the commentaries of Samkara and others'; Vedānta 'the very marrow and bones' of his doctrine; tenets 'Hinduistic, and on the philosophical side have a Vedantic basis'; socially advanced (meat, foreign travel, non-Hindus admitted). No mention of Daśanāmī initiation or Totāpurī
quote: He simply preached the old religion of India, which was founded on the Veda, more particularly on the Upa- nishads, and was systematised later on in the Siitras of Badarayana, and finally developed in the commentaries of Samkara and others.
notes: the only colonial link Ramakrishna→Śaṅkara (doctrinal, via Max Müller)

what_is_said: Vivekananda's appeal lay less in universal religion than in his effect on 'the patriotic spirit of young Hindus': 'the religion of the nationalists—the cult of India'
quote: Probably, however, it was not Vivekdénanda’s advocacy of an universal religion that appealed to Indians, so muchas his forceful character and the impression he made on the patriotio spirit of young Hindus

what_is_said: Branch of the Ramkrishna Mission which helps the distressed and relieves the sick; alongside a Brahmo Sabha and the Arya Dharma Pracharini Sabha (expounding the Śāstras)
quote: There is aleo a Beahmo Sabha at Sirajganj, as well as a branch of the Ramkrishna Mission, which helps the distressed and gives relief to the sick and suffering

institution: Sadharan Samaj and New Dispensation branches
what_is_said: Two branches with only 20 members, 5 resident; 13 Brahmos at census
quote: There are now two branches of the Brahma Samaj in the district, the SAdharan Brahma Sam4j, and the New Dispensation Church, Between them they have only twenty members

what_is_said: Listed among Patna associations with the Bihar Young Men's Institute and the Gorakshini Sabha
quote: Among other associitiong may be men- tioned the Bihar Young Men’s Institute, the Theosophical Bociety and the Gorakshini Sabha.

what_is_said: Hagiographic appendix (sources: Advaita Ashrama, Ramakrishna Math publications): Ramakrishna received monastic initiation from 'the extraordinary Vedantic monk Totapuri' who led him 'through the jnana path of Advaita', and took the name Ramakrishna in that ceremony; organised his disciples into 'a monastic order' under Vivekananda before 16 Aug 1886. Totāpurī's Daśanāmī (Purī) affiliation is not named
quote: the extraordinary Vedantic monk Totapuri. The Bhairavi led him success¬ fully through the Vaisnava and Sakta paths and Totapuri through the jnana path of Advaita. It was from the latter that Cadadhar is said to have got his name changed to Ramakrishna as part of the ceremony of monastic initiation.
notes: the only text linking Ramakrishna to an Advaita sannyāsa initiation; also in duplicate scan dli.ministry.08795; KEY ROW for the Advaita/Daśanāmī question

what_is_said: At the Ghose house at Antpur Narendranath (Vivekananda) and eight other disciples 'took a vow of Sannyasa ... over a lighted fire' on 24 Dec 1886; a temple and dispensary now at Premananda's birthplace
quote: that Naredranath Datta (later Swami Vivekananda) and eight other disciples of Sri Ramakrishna Deva took a vow of Sannyasa (renunciation of the worldly life) over a lighted fire on the night of December 24, 1886
notes: sannyāsa without reference to any Daśanāmī order

institution: Ramakrishna Math & Mission Kamarpukur and affiliated bodies
what_is_said: Kamarpukur branch 1947 (preserves birthplace; temple, higher secondary school, nursery and basic schools, guest houses, area library); Sri Ramakrishna Sarada Vidyamahapith college 1959; Hooghly District Ramakrishna Seva Sangha 1952 (assets c. Rs 1,00,000); Mahesh Ramakrishna Asram 1952; Prabuddha Bharat Sangha Itachuna 1940; Satpathabalambi Sampradaya c.1902 to 'translate the ideals of Ramkrishna-Vivekananda into action' (turned political after 1905)
quote: The Kamarpukur (Goghat P.S.) branch of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission was founded in 1947 for preserving the ancestral house where Sri Ramakrishna Paramahansa was born.

what_is_said: Rammohan's Vedāntagrantha (1815), Vedāntasāra and Upaniṣad translations: 'deeply influenced by Samkara and mainly sticks to the latter's position' except greater stress on upāsanā, liberation within reach of householders 'and no monopoly of sanyasins', and maya as God's creative power; 'adherence to Advaita-Vedanta'; Brahmo Samaj founded 1828
quote: In his interpretation of the Vedanta he has been deeply influenced by Samkara and mainly sticks to the latter’s position except on three points
notes: explicit Śaṅkara link for the Brahmo founder, framed against sannyāsin monopoly; duplicate scan dli.ministry.08795

what_is_said: Tattvabodhini Pathsala opened 1843 at Debendranath's instance, closed 1846 'due to adverse propaganda by orthodox Hindus against its Brahmo sponsors' (cf. 1912: boys becoming 'Vedantists')
quote: the Tatwabodhini Sabha opened the Tatwabodhini Pathsala at Bansberia in 1843 which had to be wound up in 1846 due to adverse propaganda by orthodox Hindus against its Brahmo sponsors.
notes: Bansberia also native place of P.C. Mozoomdar; Keshab's Sadhan Kanan at Rishra; Brahmos in 1961 census lumped with 'others' (17)

what_is_said: Brahmo convert to Christianity who attacked Vivekananda 'for adding one more divinity in the person of Ramakrishna to the Hindu pantheon' and Annie Besant for misrepresenting the Vedas; later preached Vedantism in England 1902–03
quote: Through the columns of the Sophia he attacked not only Vivekananda for adding one more divinity in the person of Ramakrishna to the Hindu pantheon, but also Annie Besant
notes: inter-reform polemic (Brahmo/Christian vs Ramakrishna and Theosophy)

institution: Belur Math, HQ of the Ramakrishna Order
what_is_said: Appendix 'The Ramakrishna Math and Mission: its ideals and activities' (from Mission reports): order founded 19 Oct 1886 at Baranagar 'to raise a band of sannyasi teachers of Vedanta'; Mission association 1 May 1897; Belur land bought 1898 for Rs 39,000; consecrated 9 Dec 1898; HQ from 1 Jan 1899; trust deed 1901; registered society 1909; 115 branch centres (52 Mission, 19 combined, 44 Math) + 22 sub-centres; 1964-65: 11 hospitals with 1,259 beds, 65 dispensaries; 1966 schools with 44,368 boys and 18,535 girls; refugee relief Rs 2,38,000
quote: Shortly after his passing away, a monastic order bearing his name was set up on October 19, 1886 at Baranagar, two miles north of Calcutta, by his disciples headed by Swami Vivekananda. Its ideal was to raise a band of sannyasi teachers of Vedanta
notes: 'sannyasi teachers of Vedanta' but no mention of Daśanāmī/Purī affiliation or of Śaṅkara; duplicate scan dli.ministry.08796 not present

institution: Ramakrishna Mission educational institutions; Ramakrishna Vivekananda Ashrama
what_is_said: Vidyamandira residential college (1940–41; Rs 10,000 from Miss Macleod), Saradapitha 1941, Sikshanamandira teachers' college 1958 (125 trainees 1965-66, Rs 1,23,000 grant), Silpamandira polytechnic, Silpavidyalaya, Jnanasikshamandira 1949; Ramakrishna Vivekananda Ashrama Kasundia founded 1916 by Swami Sivananda with daily Ramakrishna worship and festivals incl. Sivaratri, Kali Puja, Christmas Eve
quote: In 1939, the Belur Math and Mission (Ramakrishna Mission) decided to set up a residential college within the Math campus in Belur (P.S. Baly).

what_is_said: Belur Math 'perhaps represents the most potent force in living memory for a religious and cultural regeneration of modern India'; the movement 'crystallized today into a dynamic religious institution' — presented as the culmination of the Bengal renaissance after the Brahmo Samaj
quote: stands the Belur Math, the headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission, which perhaps represents the most potent force in living memory for a religious and cultural regeneration of modern India.
notes: same chapter treats the Daśanāmī Bhot-bagan (Puran Giri) separately as history

what_is_said: Brahmoism in Howrah 'thrived only in the rural areas': 85 Brahmos in 1901 (45 m, 40 f), 63 in 1961 (23 urban, 40 rural); Fakirdas Ray founded a New Dispensation Samaj and school at Amragori; Santragachi Samaj 1858–64 closed 'owing to want of support'; Brahmo prayer hall at Amragori
quote: It is curious that Brahmoism in the district thrived only in the rural areas. In 1901 there were 85 Brahmos in the district, of whom 45 were males and 40 females.
notes: religion chapter quotes a Marxian-style evaluation of the Samaj as attack on 'religious feudalism' and 'the thraldom of the priestly classes'

volume: Bihar DG Shahabad (revised, P.C. Roy Choudhury) [dli.ministry.07467]
institution: Arya Samaj Arrah (Shradhanand Bhawan; Bihar Rajya Arya Pratinidhi Sabha)
what_is_said: Established in district 1878; 12 important centres, 5 middle + 7 primary boys' schools, 6 girls' schools, 20 libraries, 10 Vedic Arya Samaj Mandirs; elsewhere 38 units; Arrah building is State HQ of the Bihar Rajya Arya Pratinidhi Sabha; Arya and Hindu Mahasabha intervention blamed for the Sasaram riot of 24 Nov 1936
quote: There are 12 important centres of the Arya Samaj in the district situated at Arrah, Jagdishpur, Piro, Lasarhi, Buxar, Dehri- on-Sone, Koilwar, Bhabua, Ramgarh, Mohania, Agiaon and Sasaram.
notes: duplicate scan dli.csl.3148

what_is_said: Revised framing: Arya, Brahmo and Theosophy 'more a reorientation of Hinduism', not opposed to its basic ideas; 'The followers of Dayanand Saraswati or the Arya Samaj are believers of monism' while Brahmos follow 'monotheism of the Upanishads'; Keshab Sen lionised by the Maharaja of Dumraon with the Raja's guru Naga Baba presiding
quote: the creed of Arya Samaj, the Brahmo Samaj or the school of Theosophy was more a reorientation of Hinduism. They gave different interpretations and it will not be correct to say that they were opposed to the basic ideas of Hinduism.
notes: reform/brahmo/arya/theosophy; contrast with colonial 'opposition' framing; 'monism' for Arya is an error

what_is_said: Keshab Sen's Bihar tours from 1867 set up Brahmo mandirs; Arrah centre attended by orthodox Hindus and Muslims; Bihari Hindus joined; Sivanath Sastri visited Arrah four times; centre 'has declined as most of the Brahmos there either left the place or died'
quote: The Brahmo Samaj Centre at Arrah as such has declined as most of the Brahmos there ¢ither left the place or diced.

what_is_said: Lodge founded at Arrah 1899 by students of 'Theosophy or Brahma Vidya' led by lawyer Kailash Chandra Banerjee; study classes, lectures; new lodges at Dehri-on-Sone and Buxar
quote: A lodge of the ‘Theosophical Soctety was founded at Arvah in 1899 by a group of enthusiastic studeats of “Vheosopky or Brahma Vidya headed by the then leading lawyer Shri Kailash Chandra Banerjee.

what_is_said: Branches at Monghyr and Jamalpur 1864; Monghyr Mandir built 1868 on Government land, holds part of Keshab Sen's ashes; Keshab's 'second home'; library, night school for depressed classes; women left purdah; social activities 'rather on a decadent' by 1959
quote: The Brahmo Mandir at Monghyr has preserved the ashes of Keshab Chandra Sen.

institution: Sanatan Dharma Sabha, Monghyr (Krishna Prasanna Sen / Paribrajak Krishnananda)
what_is_said: Krishna Prasanna Sen, initiated by Dayal Das Swami of the Punjab, published 'Dharma Pracharak' (1874), set up a Sanatan Dharma Sabha 'as counterpoise to the Brahmo Samaj' which still maintains a Sanskrit college; moved HQ to Varanasi 1882; Rani Saraswati Sanatan Dharma Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya (1866) taken over by Government 1954
quote: Krishna Prasanna had also set up at Monghyr a Sanatan Dharma Sabha as counterpoise to the Brahmo Samaj.
notes: sanatan_dharma_sabha; no Śaṅkara seat named

institution: Arya Samaj Monghyr; Arya Upa-Pratinidhi Sabha
what_is_said: Dayānand visited 1872–73, Lekhram later; Samaj 1897; branches; Gogri Arya Samaj 'burnt to ashes in 1919'; śuddhi/reconversion, Santal uplift; Upa-Pratinidhi Sabha for Bhagalpur division 1939
quote: Like the Brahmo pioneers, the Arya Samaji leaders also suffered a lot because of their advanced views.on society and religion. The Gogri Arya Samaj was burnt to ashes in 1919.

what_is_said: Ramakrishna visited Monghyr shortly before his death; 'hundreds of adherents' of Ramakrishna and Vivekananda now
quote: Swami Ram Krishna Paramhansa had visited Monghyr a few years before his ascension and there are at the moment hundreds of adherents of Swami Ram Krishna Paramhansa and his great disciple Swami Vivekananda.
notes: Ramakrishna's visit to Monghyr is not otherwise attested

what_is_said: Founded 22 Feb 1864; building 1880 (Raja Shib Chandra Banerjee), dedicated by Keshab 1881; K.D. Ghosh (Aurobindo's father) member; Mokshada girls' school 1868; trust deed 1916; Mandir damaged 1934 and rebuilt; once 'a main centre' of Brahmo activity, now few families; some Muslim families converted
quote: The Bhagalpur Brahmo Samaj was, at one time, a main centre of the Brahmo Samaj activities in the country and helped considerably the cultural advancement of the district.
notes: same 'monism'/'monotheism of Upanishads' boilerplate as Shahabad/Saran

what_is_said: Organised April 1959, affiliated 1960; homoeopathic dispensary, junior high school, Sharir Shiksha Kendra (24 trained 1960); Vivekananda birthday celebrated with nagar sankirtan
quote: The Rama Krishna Missioi Ashram was organised in April, 1959 and was affiliated in 1960
notes: Arya Samaj Mandir Bhagalpur 1910 (p. 575); Arya protest over Hindu–Muslim marriage 1946 (communal tension)

institution: Arya Samaj Siwan; Chapra Theosophical Lodge; Seva Sadan
what_is_said: Arya Samaj Mandir Siwan 1898; D.A.V. schools to degree college; gurukul-pattern Balvikash Bhawan; widow and orphan protection samitis; widow remarriages yearly; Chapra Theosophical Lodge (branch of Bihar Federation, Patna, under Varanasi HQ) founded a Seva Sadan 1957
quote: The Arya Samaj Mandir was established in Siwan in 1898 and later its followers spread throughout the district.
notes: theosophy coded in same row; boilerplate 'Arya ... believers of monism'

institution: Ramakrishna Matha, Puri (in Appendix III 'List of Mathas')
what_is_said: In the Jagannath chapter's list of Puri maths with their 'Type, Sect (Sampradaya)', the Ramakrishna Matha is classed as 'Dashnami Sannyasi', next to the Sankarananda math ('Dandi Sannyasi') and 'Sankaracharya or Bhogabardhan' (do.) — the only text in the sample that files a Ramakrishna house under the Daśanāmī order
quote: Rima Chhatra Khairata Rani Matha do. Runi Matha Goudiya Ramakrishna Matha Dashnami Sannyasi Sankarananda Dandi Sannyasi Sankaracharya or Bhogabardhan do.
notes: OCR breaks the two-column table into alternating name/sect lines; pairing inferred from neighbours (Ranganaikachari=Ramanuj, Bhogabardhan=Dandi). KEY ROW for the Daśanāmī question

institution: Ramakrishna Math & Mission Bhubaneswar; Ramakrishna Mission Ashrama Puri
what_is_said: Bhubaneswar branch founded 1919 by Swami Brahmananda (first President), building 1923; dispensary (1919), ME school, UP school, Vivekananda public library (1963, 11,547 vols); Puri Ashrama from 1944, free primary school 1933, Vivekananda ME school 1963; Mission library Puri 1925 (10,000 vols); listed 'among the existing well-known Mathas' of Bhubaneswar
quote: Among the existing well-known Mathas, a branch of the Ramakrishna Matha and Mission at Bhubaneshwar established in 1919 by Swami Brahmananda Maharaj, the first President of the organisation, is well known.

institution: Brahmo Mandir 'Universal Religious Mission of the New Dispensation'
what_is_said: 'Microscopic section'; mandir established 1930 with Calcutta Brahmos who summer in Puri; Sunday Vedic readings; observe Samaj foundation day and Rammohun's birthday
quote: There is a Brahmo Mandira in Puri town named as “Universal Religious Mission of the New Dispensation”. This was established in the year 1930

what_is_said: Dayānand visited 1869 and 'held public discussions on religion with the leading pundits of the city including Madhava Acharya and Anand Acharya who represent Hindu orthodoxy'; founded an institution at Kedar Ghat two years later; Kalwars and Bhats attracted; Aryas: 0 (1891), 176 (1901), 311 (1951); Arya Samaj Anathalaya, DAV Degree College
quote: In 1869, Dayanand Saraswati (who had founded the Arya Samaj sect a year earlier) visited Varanasi and throughout his stay held public dis¬ cussions on rcligon with the leading pundits of the city including Madhava Acharya and Anand Adharya who represent Hindu orthodoxy.
notes: orthodox opponents named as 'Acharyas', not as a Śaṅkara maṭha

institution: Theosophical Society Indian Section HQ; Central Hindu College; Vasanta College
what_is_said: Branch opened 28 Dec 1890, Indian HQ moved from Madras five years later on c.26 bighas bought by Besant; members 'for a time closely affiliated with the Arya Samaj of Varanasi for the purpose of reviving Hindu culture'; CHC 1898 with Bhagwan Das; Vasanta College (Theosophical National School) 1913; Ranbir Sanskrit Pathshala 1901; Besant Theosophical HSS; theosophy described neutrally in the religion chapter
quote: The members of the society were for a time closely affiliated with the Arya Samaj of Varanasi for the purpose of reviving Hindu culture.
notes: Bharat Dharma Mahamandal (6,000 members in 1909 Nevill) absent from the 1965 volume

institution: Ramakrishna Mission Home of Service hospital
what_is_said: Started 1900, registered 1909 as Mission branch; 123 beds; 1960-61 expenditure Rs 1,96,193
quote: Ramakrishna Mission Home of Service (Charitable Hospital), Vara¬ nasi—Although it was started in 1900 this institution was registered in 1909 as a branch of the Ramakrishna Mission.
notes: cf. Nevill 1909: income Rs 3,000; no mention of the Advaita Ashrama Varanasi

institution: Advaita Ashrama Mayavati; Sri Ramkrishna Kutir Almora
what_is_said: Established by the Ramkrishna Math, Belur: Advaita Ashrama started 1899 (library >7,500 vols, 84 magazines, 23-bed charitable hospital treating >17,000 patients 1966-67); Prabuddha Bharata published at Mayavati
quote: The Ramkrishna Math, Belur (Howrah), has established the Advaita Ashram at Mayavati and the Sri Ramkrishna Kutir at Almora.
notes: 'Advaita' appears only as an institution name; no doctrinal or Daśanāmī comment

what_is_said: Dayānand visited early 1870s (stayed with Golwalkar's father); Samaj established 1895, registered 1907; Gorakhpur branch 1938 with Mahila Arya Samaj, Arya Kumar Sabha, Bal Arya Samaj; girls' HSS; affiliated to Arya Pratinidhi Sabha MP & Vidarbha; Ramkrishna Ashram Jabalpur 1946 (dispensary, library); census tables lumped 'Hindu Arya and Hindu Brahmo' with Hindus 1901–31
quote: The Arya Samaj was established at Jabalpur in the year 1895 and was registered in 1907. In 1938, a branch of the Samaj was opened in Gorakhpur ward in the city
notes: religion chapter defines traditional Hindu belief as 'Sanatan Dharm'

institution: Shri Ramkrishna Sewa Samiti / Vivekanand Ashram, Raipur
what_is_said: Samiti affiliated to Ramkrishna Mission since 1957: Vivekanand Vidyarthi Bhavan (55 students), Vivekanand Memorial Library (6,500 books 1964-65), charitable dispensary, Panchayati Raj Training Centre (c.2,000 trainees); Vivek Jyoti quarterly 1964; Vivekananda's boyhood stay in Raipur commemorated; Arya Samaj Raipur from 1914 (weekly havan; Rs 1,660 to National Defence Fund 1962)
quote: Affiliated to Shri Ramkrishna Mission, the Samiti has been functioning at Raipur since 1957 for the all round welfare of the society in general and the © youth in particular

what_is_said: Brahmo workers opened an Upasana Mandir in Mangalore 1870, reorganised as Brahmo Samaj 1903; not large but 'a considerable number of persons'; district list of movements: Arya, Brahmo, Ramakrishna Mission, Theosophical Society, Yogoda Satsang, Chinmaya Mission, Bahai; Ranganathananda of the RK Mission a native
quote: The workers of the Brahmo Samaj visited this district as long ago as 1870 and opened an Upasana Mandir in Mangalore with a number of local members.
notes: Śṛṅgeri's home region; Brahmos here were Gauḍa Sārasvata/Bunt reformers (not stated in text)

institution: Ramakrishna Mission Balakashram; Ramakrishna Seva Samaj Puttur
what_is_said: Balakashram 1951 (277 students helped); Puttur Seva Samaj 1953 (Sharadamani orphanage, Vivekananda Library, Nivedita balawadi 1969); Arya Samaj ran a sevashram (147 children in 1978) until 1968
quote: Shri Ramakrishna Mission Balakashram, Mangaladevi Road, Mangalore, was started in 1951 to house poor and meritorious students
notes: arya_samaj sevashram coded here too (Swami Sadananda Saraswati)
